newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo jumps ahead of Johnnic news.
newsitem.headline: Anglo jumps ahead of Johnnic news.

text.p: Shares in Anglo American of South Africa Ltd climbed just before close of trade, ahead of a joint announcement with the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), to finish over three percent higher on the day.
Anglo said on Wednesday it would hold a joint news conference with the NEC at 1500 GMT.
The announcement follows intense speculation that the two sides have finally reached agreement for the NEC to buy Anglo's 48 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd.
Dealers said shares had been riding high throughout trade in line with the rest of the all-share index which finished 63.6 percent higher.
"The deal hasn't been announced yet, so it is all in anticipation. You have to keep in mind Anglo is part of the the all-share index which has been soaring all day," a dealer said.
Dealers said that the market viewed the Johnnic deal as "good news" for Anglo, although Johnnic shares appeared to take a knock.
Johnnic, which reeases results on Wednesday, closed 225 cents or 3.86 points lower at 56 rand.
Anglo traded small volumes with only 39,200 shares changing hands. Johnnic volumes were larger with 53,600 shares trading.
Should the deal go ahead it will be by far the largest black empowerment venture to date.
Johnnic's assets include stakes in South African Breweries, Toyota South Africa, Premier Group and Times Media.
